instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Brush a 9 by 5 inch loaf pan with a little oil and line it with a strip of parchment that hangs over the two long sides.
Empty both pots of yogurt into a big bowl, about 1 cup. Rinse one pot and dry it well. It's your measuring cup from here on.
Add the 2 eggs, 2 pots of sugar (1 cup), 1 pot of oil (1/2 cup) and the 1 tsp vanilla. Finely grate in the zest of the lemon. Whisk until it's smooth and pale.
In a second bowl, stir together 4 pots of flour (2 cups), the 1 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt.
Transfer the flour mix into the wet bowl and fold it in with a spatula. Stop as soon as you can't see any dry flour. Overmixing makes the cake tough.
Scrape the batter into the pan and smooth the top. Bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until the top is golden and cracked and a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then lift it out by the parchment and cool it on a rack for at least 20 minutes before you slice it.
This makes 8 slices. Serve it in thick slices. Wrap what's left and keep it at room temperature for up to 3 days.
method_notes: All three are one-bowl oil cakes with plain yogurt, eggs, sugar and flour, lifted with baking powder, mixed only until the flour disappears and baked at about 350°F until a skewer comes out clean. Sundaybaker bakes a loaf for 50 to 55 minutes with 1 cup each of yogurt and sugar, 1/2 cup oil and 2 cups flour, which is exactly the classic pot ratio when the pot holds 1/2 cup, so this one measures by the pot. Baking Like a Chef keeps the traditional 1 pot yogurt, 2 pots sugar, 1 pot oil and 3 pots flour with vanilla sugar in a round pan. Chocolate & Zucchini cuts the sugar and oil, adds a spoon of rum and bakes a round cake for 30 to 35 minutes.
